name: airband
description: See every Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI chat in one place, and let them share what they did. A map of your code for agents, ready-made commands, and your plan limits.

enumDescriptions: About 2k tokens of the conversation on connecting
About 6k tokens of the conversation on connecting
About 15k tokens of the conversation on connecting
airband.contextSize.description: How much of a chat's conversation another chat gets when the two are connected. The rest is always in its flightlog, which the other chat can read.

airband.autoDeliver.description: When a connected chat finishes a reply, give it the updates that arrived while it worked right away. That costs it an extra turn (and its tokens) just to read them. Off (the default): updates wait for its next message, at no extra cost.

airband.notices.description: Show a short line in your agent's window when a chat starts (Airband is on, the map is ready, who it shares with, what other chats did here lately) and when another chat's work is added to your message. Shown to you only: it costs no tokens. Claude Code and Gemini CLI.

airband.writing.docs.description: When a chat is asked for a doc (a PRD, a spec, a README, a PR description), add Airband's short writing rules once: one idea per sentence, active voice, no hype words. After an agent writes a doc file, Airband checks it. A project's .airband.json can set this for the whole team.

airband.writing.messages.description: When a chat is asked for a message (Slack, email, a PR comment, an announcement), add Airband's short message rules once: the point first, who does what by when, at most 5 items in a list.

airband.writing.beforeSend.description: Before an agent sends a Slack message, an email, a PR or a commit, check the words. If they break the rules, Airband holds the send once and tells the agent what to fix. The same words sent again go through. Claude Code and Gemini CLI.

airband.writing.replies.description: Ask every chat for short replies you can act on: the answer or next action first, numbered steps, where things stand, no recap.

airband.codeMap.enabled.description: Keep a code map of each open folder, so AI chats can find code in a few hundred tokens instead of searching and opening files. Built by a parser on this computer (no AI), kept in ~/.airband/codemap, about 1 MB for a large repo.

airband.backupFolder.description: A folder to back up the session logs and your own commands to, every half hour (for example a folder in iCloud Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox). Empty: no backup. The code map isn't backed up; it's rebuilt from the code in seconds.

scripts.install:vscode: npm run build && vsce package --no-dependencies && node scripts/install-vscode.mjs
scripts.publish:npm: npm run pack:npm && npm publish ./npm-dist --access public
scripts.relay:dev: node scripts/build-relay.mjs && npm --prefix relay run dev
scripts.relay:deploy: node scripts/build-relay.mjs && npm --prefix relay run deploy
scripts.app:build: npm run app:tour && export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="${TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY:-$HOME/.tauri/airband-updater.key}" && npm --prefix desktop run tauri -- build --bundles app,dmg --target aarch64-apple-darwin && npm --prefix desktop run tauri -- build --bundles app,dmg --target x86_64-apple-darwin && node scripts/name-downloads.mjs
scripts.app:build:windows: npm run app:tour && npm --prefix desktop run tauri -- build --bundles nsis && node scripts/name-downloads.mjs
scripts.app:build:windows-on-mac: npm run app:tour && PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin:/opt/homebrew/opt/lld/bin:$PATH" npm --prefix desktop run tauri -- build --runner cargo-xwin --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --bundles nsis && node scripts/name-downloads.mjs

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Airband reads your agents' chats and edits their settings, so it runs only in folders you trust.
